markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (97%)** · Confident · Careful review

Single-class conformal set [F1], but the second model disagrees and neighbors split 3 of 5.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 97%, InSitu 3% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | {Invasive} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 98th pct | Not flagged; simulated stain degradation |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Disagrees on top class |
| Similar cases | 3/5 Invasive [F5] | Nearest is InSitu |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Scarce; largest term, but failed spot check · Unreliable
- **Gland / tubule formation** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Scarce; low score tracks invasive in concept model · Validated
- **Benign stroma or fat** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Scarce; same direction as tubules · Validated
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 2, 3, 9) · ↑ invasive · High score; spot check 3/20 · Unreliable
- **Atypical cells in ducts** (regions 2, 3) · ↓ invasive · Elevated; points toward in situ · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47 to 0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; unproven. Normal lobules and necrosis are Unreliable here.

## Could be wrong if
- Stain degradation (severity 3) distorts features; the MUSK model already disagrees on the top class.
- Nearest case is InSitu (85% similar), and only 3 of 5 neighbors are Invasive.

## Check on the slide
1. **2, 3**: Highest heatmap weight; necrosis and intraductal atypia peak here. Separate in situ from invasive.
2. **5**: Highest per-region invasive probability; confirm invasive growth pattern.
3. **8, 9, 10**: Bottom row abuts the inferior margin called tumor (430 µm, simulated) [F7].
